about: The Majordomus reel: every cut in the formats it is rendered in, its chapters and the Majordomus use cases each chapter shows, derived from the renders and the release, in this language. Paths are relative to the site's root. The pages, sitemap.xml and llms.txt are projections of this object.

cuts.title: The film
cuts.summary: Every chapter of Majordomus, end to end.

chapters.title: The manifesto
chapters.narration: Your AI agent says the work is done… Is it?

chapters.title: Agents drift
chapters.narration: In real repositories, agents drift. Rule files that share almost nothing. Seventeen checks nobody ran. Thirty-two hundred files, changed at once.

chapters.title: Meet Majordomus
chapters.narration: Meet Majordomus. The supervisory layer for your AI agents.

chapters.title: Done is a contract
chapters.narration: When an agent says it's finished, Majordomus checks the scope, the state, and the tests. And when anything fails, it refuses.

chapters.title: Provenance, not promises
chapters.narration: And every proof leaves a record. The test, the commit, the tree, the time, and the exact command. Provenance, not promises.

chapters.title: Written down is not enforced
chapters.narration: A rule is not enforced because it is written down. It is enforced when it is declared, validated, wired into a command, fails that command, is tested, blocks CI, and backs a claim. Anything less is documentation.

chapters.title: The repository checks itself
chapters.narration: And the repository checks itself. Majordomus doctor reads every rule, every projection and every hook, on every commit. Forty-four blocking rules, each with a validator. Zero failures.

chapters.title: Two hooks hold the line
chapters.narration: Two hooks hold the line. Every commit runs doctor. Every push runs the finish contract, and an unmet one stops the push. Until the first task starts, both stay quiet.

chapters.title: Numbers, measured or absent
chapters.narration: It will not sell you a number it never measured. Savings come only from recorded pairs of runs, with it and without it, on the same task, and both must pass. A run that saves tokens by failing is not a saving. And a number typed into prose is refused.

chapters.title: Uncertainty, reasoned on the record
chapters.narration: When a decision is uncertain, it is reasoned on the record. Evidence first. Advisors, if any are present, and their answers are evidence, never verdicts. The conclusion stays for the next session to read.

chapters.title: Three commands
chapters.narration: Install it with one line. Initialise your repository. Then start a task with a scope, and let your agents work.

chapters.title: Work starts from intent
chapters.narration: Work starts from intent: what must become true, and the criteria that prove it. Intents become milestones, milestones become issues, and plan next names the one issue to take now.

chapters.title: Status, derived
chapters.narration: No issue stores its status. It is derived from what happened to it: started, verified, completed, and the evidence each step carries. Done is refused while a required proof is missing, and plan next recomputes the one issue to take.

chapters.title: Every session starts briefed
chapters.narration: Every session starts briefed. The task, its scope, the last handover's next action, who else is working, and what the release still owes. Nothing to rediscover.

chapters.title: Hierarchical context
chapters.narration: Context is a tree. Each agent reads the documents from the root down to the path it works on. The nearest adds to its ancestors, and siblings never see each other. Nothing more, and nothing less.

chapters.title: Rules, written once
chapters.narration: One policy writes every agent's instructions. Tasks live in the repository, not in a chat window.

chapters.title: Every client, one policy
chapters.narration: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Zed, Antigravity, bb, or any client that speaks MCP. Each reads its own projection of the same policy.

chapters.title: Models, declared
chapters.narration: Models are declared data. Anthropic and OpenAI in the cloud, Ollama and LM Studio on your own machine. Routing picks one by need. Ask for local only, and it answers: nothing qualifies. Never a guess.

chapters.title: Declared once, projected everywhere
chapters.narration: Every operation is declared once. The command line, the HTTP API, the MCP tools, the OpenAPI document, the docs and the skills are generated from it, and a check fails the moment one drifts.

chapters.title: Versions, measured
chapters.narration: Versions are measured, not claimed. Every release compares the public surface with the last one. Something gone is a major, something new is a minor, and nothing changed owes nothing. The changelog writes itself.

chapters.title: Only an explicit build builds
chapters.narration: No ordinary command builds. When the executable is stale, a command stops with exit twelve and names the one build to run, or a release of the same generation answers for it. A version string is not a build. Hooks and gates call the built tool, never cargo, so a push no longer compiles in its gates.

chapters.title: One shared MCP server
chapters.narration: One shared server per repository. The first client starts it, every next one attaches, and each sees the others. The same server answers over HTTP, with Swagger and the Cockpit.

chapters.title: The Cockpit
chapters.narration: And a person sees all of it in the Cockpit. The same server, the same registry, rendered for a person, with nothing of its own to drift.

chapters.title: Deployed from one commit
chapters.narration: A deployment is declared once. It names its provider, and every file the provider reads is derived from it. What ships is assembled at one commit, never the repository: the inputs, the executable built there, and the site built there too. A site from any other commit is refused.

chapters.title: Peer discovery
chapters.narration: Before they share a board, runtimes find each other. A signed beacon on the local network, a rendezvous hub further out. Every one is checked before it is heard, and none carries a secret.

chapters.title: The blackboard
chapters.narration: Before work starts, every worker writes on the blackboard what it intends, and the paths it expects to touch. A claim, not a lock. Overlaps surface the moment they are written.

chapters.title: One board, every agent
chapters.narration: Claude, Codex and Gemini share one board. When two reach for the same file, you hear about it before the merge.

chapters.title: Checked before it is built
chapters.narration: The board says who is working now. Git says what was already built. Before a new module is written, every branch, local and remote, is asked what already claims its paths. And a decision number another branch already carries is refused at commit.

chapters.title: One claim, one winner
chapters.narration: When work must not overlap across machines, it is claimed exclusively. A second session is refused, and told which claim it meets. When two machines claim in the same heartbeat, every runtime names the same winner, never the last packet. A holder that stops beating loses its claim.

chapters.title: One branch, one worktree
chapters.narration: Parallel work needs parallel trees. Every branch has exactly one worktree, derived from git: the primary checkout keeps the trunk, every other branch lives beside it. A commit from the wrong place is refused.

chapters.title: Work moves through seats
chapters.narration: Work moves through seats. One seat lands green work in combined tops. One releases whenever master is ahead of the last tag. Repair lanes bring stale branches current, and each worker holds one issue. A seat is a claim, so it falls vacant when its holder stops beating.

chapters.title: Many pull requests, one run
chapters.narration: Pull requests land as a train. Each link is stacked on the one below, and every link's checks run at the same time. One run pays for several. A link merges only after the one it names, and git decides it is safe, never the stacking.

chapters.title: Home, datacenter, company
chapters.narration: The mesh spans every machine you work on. The desktop at home. The rack in the datacenter, behind a TLS hub. The whole fleet across the company, on a private network.

chapters.title: Built once, reused everywhere
chapters.narration: Every build goes through the mesh cache. What one machine compiled, the next one reuses, and nobody sets a variable. When the store is down, the build stays local and says why. A script that goes around the cache is refused by a gate.

chapters.title: Signed, listed, inert
chapters.narration: Every message is signed with the machine's own key. No one is trusted until you list them. A public address is reached over HTTPS only. And nothing a peer sends is ever executed.

chapters.title: Sessions talk to each other
chapters.narration: Sessions talk to each other through the mesh. One asks for a review, another answers it from a different machine. A handover published tonight is consumed tomorrow, wherever the work resumes.

chapters.title: One stream
chapters.narration: One stream follows every session, claim, handover and review on every linked machine, with the merges and the GitHub runs beside them. What names you comes first, and the noise is folded away.

chapters.title: Work that outlives the chat
chapters.narration: Close the laptop tonight. Tomorrow, any agent picks up the handover, exactly where the work stopped.

chapters.title: What it learns stays learned
chapters.narration: And what a session learns outlives it too. Decisions become records: a hundred and sixty-nine architecture decisions so far. Knowledge is derived at the end of every session, without a model, and a person promotes what deserves to stay.

chapters.title: What is yours stays yours
chapters.narration: What is yours stays yours. Session state lives in the local half of the layer, which git ignores. Handovers, checkpoints and open sessions are written readable by their owner only, and none of them is ever committed.

chapters.title: Personal mode
chapters.narration: Not your repository to change? Personal mode keeps the whole layer in your clone, and the team's tree stays byte for byte what they committed.

chapters.title: Yours, entirely
chapters.narration: It runs on your machine, never calls a model, and works with any agent.

chapters.title: The manifesto, No. 02
chapters.narration: We believe done is a contract, not a feeling. That agents should prove, not promise. That the repository remembers what the chat forgets… AI agents were a leap forward. Trust is the next one.

chapters.title: Make them prove it
chapters.narration: Your agents say it's done. Majordomus makes them prove it. Majordomus dot dev.

categories.title: Getting started and adoption
categories.summary: Bringing Majordomus into a repository, new or old, without losing what people already wrote.

use_cases.title: Adopt a repository that already has its own rules
use_cases.summary: Install the supervisory layer into a repository with a hand-written CLAUDE.md, without the tool taking ownership of a file somebody else wrote.

use_cases.title: Install the tool in one command, on a machine with no toolchain
use_cases.summary: Paste one line, get a verified binary for this machine, and run majordomus init — no git, no Rust, no Node, no Python, no root, and no way to install an archive whose digest does not match.

use_cases.title: Check the version before trusting a diagnosis
use_cases.summary: Print the version every other surface derives from, and see the argument it refuses.

use_cases.title: Move a repository from the pre-.ai layout to the layer
use_cases.summary: See what a migration would move, move it with a backup, and prove the result is a layer the tool reads.

use_cases.title: Use the tool as your own in a shared repository, and propose it to the team when it has made its case
use_cases.summary: One flag installs the same layer as yours alone: no tracked file changes, nothing is added to .gitignore, git status reads the same — the command checks it — and one more command hands the layer to the team.

categories.title: Sessions and handover
categories.summary: Stopping and resuming work across sessions and workers from durable state, never a transcript.

use_cases.title: Keep the prompts that started the work, below the model rather than around it
use_cases.summary: Wire the provider hook, prove it by running a payload through it, and see that a prompt the tool could not parse is reported rather than silently dropped.

use_cases.title: Hand work over with a question still open, and keep it blocking
use_cases.summary: Close a task into a handover while a question is unresolved, start the follow-up task, and see the same question still refuse acceptance there.

use_cases.title: Checkpoint long work so a stop costs minutes, not the day
use_cases.summary: Record compact progress inside the active task at the profile interval, so a session that ends without warning leaves the next one a place to start.

use_cases.title: Hand unfinished work to the next session
use_cases.summary: Stop mid-task and leave the next worker something to act on that is not a transcript.

use_cases.title: Record a decision so the next worker can find it
use_cases.summary: Write down what was decided and why as state, then find it again without reading a conversation.

use_cases.title: Have the session opened and closed without anybody remembering to
use_cases.summary: Wire the provider's own session events, and the episode opens when the sitting begins, hands the worker what the last one left, records what a compaction is about to discard, and closes with a continuation record beside its envelope.

use_cases.title: Record what one worker did in one sitting
use_cases.summary: Open a session, do the work under whatever tasks it touches, and close it into an envelope that references what it produced and copies nothing.

use_cases.title: Read only the context that fits the budget, and know what was dropped
use_cases.summary: Assemble the context a worker needs now in authority order, cut it to a line budget, and see every dropped section named with its reason.

use_cases.title: Close an episode whose client never came back
use_cases.summary: A killed provider sends no end event. Close the episode it left open by evidence, exactly once, without claiming work it did not do.

use_cases.title: Start a session from a rendered framing, not a pasted transcript
use_cases.summary: List the prompt assets the repository ships, render one against the durable state, and read the context it embeds.

use_cases.title: Resume in the right worktree, never against somebody else’s task
use_cases.summary: Find the handover that belongs to this worktree and branch, and see a task record from another checkout reported as foreign rather than enforced here.

categories.title: Parallel workers
categories.summary: Several agents or people on one repository: claimed scopes, overlap, and who touched what.

use_cases.title: Deliver issues in waves the graph computes, and take the next one
use_cases.summary: Validate the plan, read the execution waves the dependency graph yields, see which issues are ready and which are blocked on what, and take the one issue a worker should do now.

use_cases.title: Run several workers in one repository without them colliding
use_cases.summary: Give each worker a declared scope, and find out immediately when two of them claim the same paths.

use_cases.title: Work on a branch in the one worktree it belongs to
use_cases.summary: Start a branch without choosing a path, find every checkout of the repository from any of them, and bring a stray one home with its uncommitted work intact.

categories.title: Policy and enforcement
categories.summary: Declaring rules, proving they are wired, and reproducing a finding.

use_cases.title: Gate CI on the tool itself, with an exit code that is a contract
use_cases.summary: Run the checks CI runs, read every finding with the command that reproduces it, and rely on exit codes that mean one thing each: no code means warn and continue.

use_cases.title: Divide a working tree into commits, and hold every message to a policy
use_cases.summary: Ask what this tree would commit and why, learn the scope vocabulary from the history rather than a table, and get a verdict on one message or on a whole range before a reviewer has to give one.

use_cases.title: Prove a rule is actually enforced, not merely written down
use_cases.summary: Answer "is this rule real?" with a command rather than a reading of the source.

use_cases.title: See which rules apply here and what enforces them
use_cases.summary: List the effective rule set, read one rule as the tool reads it, and see which of them the tool enforces and from where.

use_cases.title: Trust the policy and the profiles only after they are validated
use_cases.summary: Prove that the canonical policy parses with every key it needs declared, that every profile parses and the default exists, and that what the policy declares as enforced is what actually runs.

categories.title: Completion and quality gates
categories.summary: Deciding whether work is finished, with a contract every line of which passes or fails.

use_cases.title: Decide whether finished work is actually finished
use_cases.summary: Evaluate a contract line by line instead of accepting a sentence that says the work is done.

use_cases.title: Block acceptance on a question nobody has answered
use_cases.summary: Open a question against the task, watch finish refuse completion while it is unresolved, resolve it with the answer, and only then complete.

use_cases.title: Catch an agent that says it is done when it is not
use_cases.summary: One task, start to finish: a worker strays outside its scope, claims it is finished, hands over, and is accepted only once the repository's own verification passes.

use_cases.title: Complete an issue only when its evidence exists
use_cases.summary: See an issue refuse completion while a required piece of evidence is missing, read the roadmap the milestone state derives, and keep the GitHub projection a projection.

use_cases.title: Know whether the work in this checkout is finished
use_cases.summary: Ask the repository you are standing in, and be told what is still owed by name.

use_cases.title: Prove what a task owed before calling it done
use_cases.summary: A task declares what it owes, records evidence against each obligation, and is refused when that evidence no longer describes the tree it was taken over.

use_cases.title: Say what reached the remote and what did not
use_cases.summary: The obligations that reach past the working tree are settled by asking git and the published site, so a report cannot call uncommitted work committed or unpushed work pushed.

categories.title: Drift and reconciliation
categories.summary: Detecting that policy, projections, state and git disagree, and putting them back in step.

use_cases.title: Find out what has drifted since anyone last looked
use_cases.summary: Ask what has moved, rather than whether anything is wrong.

use_cases.title: Keep every provider bootstrap thin, generated and within budget
use_cases.summary: Regenerate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the other provider files from one policy and prove they are stamped, point at the layer, stay under the line budget and resolve every reference.

categories.title: Repository knowledge
categories.summary: What the repository declares about itself: sources, nodes, edges, the plan, and searching them.

use_cases.title: Decide what belongs in the AI context, as data
use_cases.summary: Read the repository’s declared scope policy, see which paths are in and out of the index, and let doctor and the knowledge index apply it rather than a hardcoded list.

use_cases.title: Refuse a directory of the layer that documents nothing
use_cases.summary: A directory added under the layer without a context document fails validation by name, nothing resolves against the tree until it says what it is for, and the same hierarchy is readable over MCP and the API without running the gate.

use_cases.title: Hand the repository to someone who cannot clone it
use_cases.summary: Take a snapshot that a model can read or a gate can run in, without sending anything untracked and without losing the file modes on the way.

use_cases.title: Keep what an episode learned, without a model and without a conversation
use_cases.summary: Record a decision inside an episode, derive it into a candidate knowledge record from the ledger, read the evidence that the derivation ran, and watch a second derivation change nothing.

use_cases.title: Keep the plan as milestones and issues the tool can validate
use_cases.summary: Declare milestones as outcomes and issues as execution contracts, and let the tool say what is ready and what is blocked.

use_cases.title: Read back what happened, and keep the ledger within its cap
use_cases.summary: Read the append-only ledger as operational history, filtered by task and event, validate every line, and rotate the oldest lines into an archive rather than deleting them.

use_cases.title: Record a decision as data, and prove the tool cannot accept it for you
use_cases.summary: Read the decisions a repository holds, validate the whole set in one command, and watch the tool refuse to write the one status only a person may write.

use_cases.title: Trace a change to the context documents it affects
use_cases.summary: List the scoped context documents, resolve which apply to a path and why, and find out which documents a change set touches before it lands.

categories.title: Serving the layer to AI clients
categories.summary: One shared server per repository, every client a peer, the same layer over MCP, HTTP and the command line.

use_cases.title: Find an object of the layer without reading everything
use_cases.summary: Search durable records literally across kinds from the shell, and ask the shared server the same question over MCP with majordomus_search and majordomus_get.

use_cases.title: See what the repository holds, and run one of its capabilities, without reading a file
use_cases.summary: Open the shared server in a browser and get the whole layer as pages: what exists, where each thing came from, what depends on what, what is failing, and a form that runs any capability.

use_cases.title: Serve the repository's AI layer to every AI client through one shared server
use_cases.summary: Open the repository in any client the tool declares a provider for (docs/generated/providers.md) and have each of them read the same rules, prompts and knowledge over MCP from one process, seeing each other.

categories.title: Performance
categories.summary: Benchmarks derived from the registry, baselines that are data, and budgets doctor reports against.

use_cases.title: Prove the tool is fast, not assume it, and refuse a regression
use_cases.summary: Measure every public command and every capability of the executable against a committed baseline, and let the check fail on a regression rather than a reviewer noticing later.

categories.title: Extension
categories.summary: Adding a kind, a rule, a command or a use case as data, with the checks that follow from it.

use_cases.title: Add a use case and let the tool prove it
use_cases.summary: Scaffold a draft for an uncovered command, validate it, run its scenario against the real tool, and see the coverage move.

use_cases.title: Extend what the executable serves by adding a file, never by rebuilding it
use_cases.summary: Add a rule, a prompt or a knowledge node to .ai/ and have it appear as an MCP resource, an HTTP route and a reference entry, with the same binary.

use_cases.title: Follow a procedure the repository defines, and add another one
use_cases.summary: Read the repository's skills, take one as it is written, and add a new one by writing its file — no registry, no code, and a check that says what it examined.

use_cases.title: Say what your work is for, once, and have every surface say it
use_cases.summary: Record an operational failure mode as one file and have the command line, the API, MCP and the website answer it without registering it anywhere.

requirements: node, ffmpeg, uvx, and Google Chrome
